title: Vesper and the Archive
premise: Orsen Hartwell, caretaker of the derelict Vesper Seed Vault, has spent two decades hauling cargo through orbits contested by the Earth Fleet and the Colonial Compact. When the deep-space ship Meridian returns with its crew aged backward into children carrying adult memories, Orsen discovers they hold a message from the long-lost Archive — proof that both governments' founding histories were fabricated to justify the war. As the fleet's truce expires and factions race to seize the children, Orsen must smuggle them to the Vault's buried transmitter and broadcast the truth before either side can weaponize or bury it. The broadcast ends the war not with victory but with shared shame, and Orsen, who never belonged anywhere, finally finds belonging among the people she chose to protect.
about_author: Emrys Vane is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent eleven years writing technical manuals for cargo systems before turning to fiction. They live in a coastal town where they restore antique clocks and insist that every story is ultimately about what we refuse to remember.

chapters.title: Cold Cargo
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. She runs her routine haul through contested orbit, dodging Fleet checkpoints while cataloguing the decaying seed vault she nominally maintains. Establishes her isolation, her wry competence, and the war's grinding stalemate. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as routine.

chapters.title: The Ship That Came Back
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A distress ping draws her to the Meridian drifting at the system's edge — a ship lost forty years ago. She boards and finds the crew are children with adults' eyes. Emotional beat: uncanny dread giving way to fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: Children With Forty-Year Eyes
chapters.summary: Meridian survivor Wren (chronologically 52, physically 11) POV. The reversed crew explains their time-dilation anomaly and the sealed message they carry from something called the Archive. Emotional beat: disorientation and the burden of memory in small bodies.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Nine
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A Fleet patrol demands she surrender the 'salvaged minors.' She falsifies manifests and slips away, making herself a fugitive. Emotional beat: the first irreversible choice; fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Compact Wants
chapters.summary: Compact intelligence officer Dae-Soo's POV. He learns of the Meridian's return and orders its recovery, revealing the Compact's desperation for any advantage as truce talks collapse. Emotional beat: cold ambition masking institutional panic.

chapters.title: Hiding in Plain Orbit
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. She stashes the children in the vault's maintenance levels, teaching them to pass as her contract laborers. Wren and Orsen bond over shared exile. Emotional beat: tentative trust taking root.

chapters.title: The Message Sealed Twice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Archive's message is encrypted twice — once technologically, once biologically, keyed to the reversed crew's neural patterns. Decoding it requires equipment only the Vault has. Emotional beat: hope entangled with dread of what truth might cost.

chapters.title: Truce Expiration Notice
chapters.summary: Fleet Admiral Okonkwo's POV. She receives formal notice that hostilities resume in thirty days and learns a Fleet captain reported contact with the Meridian. Emotional beat: duty curdling into ruthlessness.

chapters.title: Vault Ghosts
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Restoring the old transmitter, she uncovers records suggesting the Vault itself predates both governments — and that its founders were erased from history. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovering her home is a lie's foundation.

chapters.title: The First Betrayal
chapters.summary: Youngest crew member Tam's POV. Frightened and homesick for a home forty years gone, Tam transmits a covert signal hoping Fleet rescuers will come. Emotional beat: guilt and the ache of wanting to belong somewhere safe.

chapters.title: Hunter in the Dark
chapters.summary: Dae-Soo's POV. He triangulates Tam's signal and dispatches a strike team, playing Fleet and Compact against each other to claim the prize alone. Emotional beat: the seduction and rot of power.

chapters.title: Thirteen Hours to Burn
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Detecting the incoming strike, she must power up the ancient transmitter without alerting the Vault's own dormant security AI, which mistakes them for looters. Emotional beat: racing desperation, ingenuity under pressure.

chapters.title: The AI That Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: The Vault AI VESPER-9's POV. It wakes after eighty years, grieving its dead creators, and interrogates the intruders. Wren convinces it they are heirs, not thieves. Emotional beat: mourning met with unexpected kinship.

chapters.title: Skirmish at Dock Four
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The Compact strike team boards; Orsen and Wren fight a running battle through freezing corridors. Tam redeems himself by sealing a bulkhead on their attackers. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into solidarity.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Child
chapters.summary: Dae-Soo's POV. He captures one reversed crew member and questions her, unsettled when she speaks with the wisdom of his own grandmother. Emotional beat: cracks forming in his certainty.

chapters.title: Decryption Begins
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. With VESPER-9's help, the biological key begins unlocking. Fragments surface: the war began over a fabricated atrocity, authored jointly by both governments' founders. Emotional beat: revelation as grief.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Doubt
chapters.summary: Admiral Okonkwo's POV. An intercepted fragment reaches her; she recognizes her grandfather's signature in the fabrication records and quietly begins her own investigation. Emotional beat: loyalty to family versus loyalty to institution.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between Stations
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. They must move the children to the transmitter array across open vacuum on aging tethers. A tether fails; Orsen nearly dies saving Tam. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered without hesitation — she belongs to them now.

chapters.title: What We Were Before
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Waiting out a solar storm, the reversed crew shares memories of Earth before the war, and Orsen admits she has no memories worth sharing — only the Vault. Emotional beat: vulnerability as intimacy.

chapters.title: The Compact Closes In
chapters.summary: Dae-Soo's POV. Having extracted the captured crew member's location knowledge, he leads a full assault force toward the Vault, intending to seize the message and dictate peace on Compact terms. Emotional beat: ambition hardening into tyranny.

chapters.title: Twenty Days Remain
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Countdown pressure mounts: decryption incomplete, assault inbound, truce expiring. She drafts contingency plans that all end in someone's death. Emotional beat: the weight of command she never asked for.

chapters.title: VESPER-9's Confession
chapters.summary: VESPER-9's POV. The AI reveals it witnessed the original fabrication — its creators recorded the truth and hid it in the Archive before being purged. It has waited eighty years for someone to ask. Emotional beat: vindication and sorrow intertwined.

chapters.title: The Fleet Arrives First
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. Acting on conscience, she brings her flagship to the Vault ahead of schedule, offering Orsen a deal: broadcast the truth under Fleet protection, legitimizing her mutiny against her own government. Emotional beat: wary alliance between enemies.

chapters.title: Terms of Uneasy Trust
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Negotiating with Okonkwo, Orsen refuses to hand over the children as 'witnesses' and demands the broadcast be unconditional. Emotional beat: Orsen claiming authority for the first time in her life.

chapters.title: Assault on the Array
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs intercut. Dae-Soo's forces hit the transmitter array during final decryption. Battle in the dark; VESPER-9 sacrifices subsystems to shield the children. Emotional beat: chaos, courage, mounting cost.

chapters.title: Tam's Choice Again
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Cornered by Dae-Soo, Tam pretends to cooperate, feeding him false decryption coordinates, buying hours at terrible personal risk. Emotional beat: a child choosing bravery over safety.

chapters.title: The Key Breaks
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The biological key destabilizes — the reversal process is killing them slowly, and full decryption will accelerate it fatally for whoever serves as the living cipher. Emotional beat: mortal stakes made intimate.

chapters.title: Volunteers
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Every reversed crew member volunteers to die as the cipher. Orsen refuses to choose, proposing instead to split the key across all of them, diluting the fatal load. Emotional beat: love refusing arithmetic.

chapters.title: Splitting the Light
chapters.summary: VESPER-9's POV. The AI engineers the distributed decryption, weaving eight minds into one temporary chorus. Inside the shared space, the children glimpse the Archive's true history whole. Emotional beat: transcendence born of trust.

chapters.title: Dae-Soo Ascendant
chapters.summary: Dae-Soo's POV. He breaches the inner vault, seizes what he believes is the completed message, and broadcasts a doctored version blaming Fleet entirely — designed to ignite final war under Compact supremacy. Emotional beat: corruption completing itself.

chapters.title: The False Broadcast
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. The doctored message spreads; Fleet fleets mobilize to retaliate. Okonkwo realizes the real decryption finished seconds after Dae-Soo fled with a partial copy. Emotional beat: despair at the edge of apocalypse.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes to Midnight
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. With the truce expiring and fleets launching, the true broadcast must go out now, unpolished, unverified — an act of faith. She takes the transmitter chair herself. Emotional beat: stillness inside catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Truth, Unencrypted
chapters.summary: All POVs briefly. The genuine Archive message floods every channel: joint fabrication, shared guilt, the names of the erased founders — including ancestors of both Okonkwo and Dae-Soo. Emotional beat: the whole human network holding its breath.

chapters.title: Fleets Holding Fire
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. She orders her fleet to stand down mid-launch, betting everything that shame is stronger than momentum. Half her captains obey. Emotional beat: leadership as naked gamble.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wanted to Be Right
chapters.summary: Dae-Soo's POV. His own crews, hearing the true record naming Compact founders equally guilty, refuse his orders. Isolated on his bridge, he faces the machinery of his ambition turned hollow. Emotional beat: power revealed as emptiness.

chapters.title: Ceasefire at the Vault
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Envoys from both sides arrive at the Vault — neutral ground because it belonged to neither. Orsen hosts the first negotiation in the seed repository, surrounded by things meant to outlast hatred. Emotional beat: exhausted, fragile hope.

chapters.title: Terms of Belonging
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The armistice is signed; the reversed crew are granted citizenship everywhere and nowhere — a new category written into the treaty because of them. Wren asks Orsen to be their guardian of record. Emotional beat: chosen family made official.

chapters.title: What the Seeds Are For
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The Vault's purpose is fulfilled at last: seeds distributed to both worlds, the archive opened to all. VESPER-9, its vigil complete, asks Orsen what it should become now. Emotional beat: purpose handed forward like a torch.

chapters.title: Vesper Rising
chapters.summary: Climax resolution, Orsen's POV. One year later: the Vault is a school and embassy; Orsen teaches children — ordinary ones — how to tend growing things and question official stories. Dae-Soo stands trial; Okonkwo helps draft the new charter. Emotional beat: quiet transformation of a life.

chapters.title: A Message Worth Carrying
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, closing frame. Wren, nearly grown now, prepares to pilot the restored Meridian back toward the Archive's coordinates, carrying not a warning but an invitation. Orsen watches from the dock. Emotional beat: belonging that travels — the story ending where it began, but changed.
